claim: Mutational antigenic profiling determines how all mutations in Env affect viral neutralization.
source: We used mutational antigenic profiling to determine how all mutations in Env affected viral neutralization and electron microscopy polyclonal epitope mapping (EMPEM) to directly visualize serum Fabs bound to Env trimers.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a method used in the study.

claim: EMPEM directly visualizes serum Fabs bound to Env trimers.
source: We used mutational antigenic profiling to determine how all mutations in Env affected viral neutralization and electron microscopy polyclonal epitope mapping (EMPEM) to directly visualize serum Fabs bound to Env trimers.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes EMPEM as a method for visualizing serum Fabs bound to Env trimers.

claim: The dominant neutralizing specificities were generally only a subset of the more diverse binding specificities.
source: The dominant neutralizing specificities were generally only a subset of the more diverse binding specificities.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Additional differences between binding and neutralization reflected antigenicity differences between virus and soluble Env trimer.
source: Additional differences between binding and neutralization reflected antigenicity differences between virus and soluble Env trimer.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and discussed in detail in the Results section.

claim: Mutational antigenic profiling and EMPEM can refine residue-level epitope specificity directly from sera.
source: Furthermore, we refined residue-level epitope specificity directly from sera, revealing subtle differences across sera.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: SOSIP trimers recapitulate the native or near-native structure of Env on the virus surface.
source: These trimers have been used extensively as immunogens because they recapitulate the native or near-native structure of Env on the virus surface (Julien et al., 2013; Lyumkis et al., 2013; Pancera et al., 2014; Sanders et al., 2013; Sanders and Moore, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Immunizing animals with BG505 SOSIP trimer variants induces autologous, tier-2 neutralizing antibody responses.
source: In general, immunizing animals with prototypical SOSIP trimer variants based on the BG505 strain (Wu et al., 2006) induces autologous, tier-2 neutralizing antibody responses (de Taeye et al., 2015; Klasse et al., 2016; Sanders et al., 2015; Torrents de la Peña et al., 2018, Torrents de la Peña et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: BG505 trimer immunization can protect against infection of simian–human immunodeficiency virus bearing the matched BG505 Env in macaques.
source: While such immunizations can protect against infection of simian–human immunodeficiency virus, bearing the matched BG505 Env in macaques (Pauthner et al., 2017; Pauthner et al., 2019), heterologous breadth has not been consistently achieved.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Heterologous breadth has not been consistently achieved with BG505 SOSIP trimer immunization.
source: While such immunizations can protect against infection of simian–human immunodeficiency virus, bearing the matched BG505 Env in macaques (Pauthner et al., 2017; Pauthner et al., 2019), heterologous breadth has not been consistently achieved.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current BG505 SOSIP trimer immunization approaches.

claim: BG505-induced rabbit neutralizing antibodies predominantly target a BG505-specific glycan hole centered on residues 241 and 289.
source: BG505-induced rabbit neutralizing antibodies predominantly target a BG505-specific glycan hole (GH) in Env's glycan shield, centered on the broadly conserved glycosylation sites at residues 241 and 289 that are missing in BG505.
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge about rabbit responses to BG505 trimer immunization.

claim: Reintroducing glycans at sites 241 and 289 eliminates much of the neutralizing activity in many rabbit serum responses.
source: Reintroducing glycans back in at these sites eliminates much of the neutralizing activity in many rabbit serum responses (Klasse et al., 2018; Klasse et al., 2016) and mAbs isolated from immunized rabbits target this immunodominant GH (McCoy et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: mAbs isolated from immunized rabbits target the immunodominant glycan hole.
source: Reintroducing glycans back in at these sites eliminates much of the neutralizing activity in many rabbit serum responses (Klasse et al., 2018; Klasse et al., 2016) and mAbs isolated from immunized rabbits target this immunodominant GH (McCoy et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The C3/V5 epitope is a frequently immunogenic site in rabbits immunized with BG505 SOSIP trimers.
source: Serum neutralization assays with large panels of pseudovirus point mutants identified a second frequently immunogenic site in rabbits as the C3/V5 epitope (previously termed C3/465), as well as a less immunodominant and less commonly targeted epitope in V1 (Klasse et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: V1 is a less immunodominant and less commonly targeted epitope in rabbits immunized with BG505 SOSIP trimers.
source: Serum neutralization assays with large panels of pseudovirus point mutants identified a second frequently immunogenic site in rabbits as the C3/V5 epitope (previously termed C3/465), as well as a less immunodominant and less commonly targeted epitope in V1 (Klasse et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: EMPEM has corroborated rabbit immunogenicity data by directly visualizing serum Fabs bound to BG505 trimer.
source: These rabbit immunogenicity data were largely corroborated using EMPEM to directly visualize serum Fabs bound to BG505 trimer bait (Bianchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In SOSIP trimer-vaccinated guinea pigs and non-human primates, antibody cloning or EMPEM has identified strain-specific responses to the C3/V4, C3/V5, V1, and gp120/gp41 interface regions.
source: In SOSIP trimer-vaccinated guinea pigs and non-human primates, antibody cloning or EMPEM has identified additional strain-specific responses to the C3/V4, C3/V5, V1, and gp120/gp41 interface regions (Cottrell et al., 2020; Lei et al., 2019; Nogal et al., 2020; Nogal et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Trimer immunization often elicits non-neutralizing responses to the base of the trimer.
source: Additionally, trimer immunization often elicits non-neutralizing responses to the base of the trimer, a neo-epitope exposed on soluble trimers but inaccessible on viral membrane-bound Env (Bianchi et al., 2018; Cottrell et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2015; Kulp et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The base of the trimer is a neo-epitope exposed on soluble trimers but inaccessible on viral membrane-bound Env.
source: Additionally, trimer immunization often elicits non-neutralizing responses to the base of the trimer, a neo-epitope exposed on soluble trimers but inaccessible on viral membrane-bound Env (Bianchi et al., 2018; Cottrell et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2015; Kulp et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Ongoing clinical trials are evaluating the immunogenicity of BG505 SOSIP trimer variants in humans.
source: Ongoing clinical trials will evaluate the immunogenicity of BG505 SOSIP trimer variants in humans (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT03699241, NCT04177355, and NCT03783130).
evidence: This claim is supported by references to clinical trial identifiers.

claim: Rabbits were sequentially vaccinated with BG505 SOSIP trimer variants: either BG505 SOSIP.664 or BG505 SOSIP.V4.1.
source: We used sera from rabbits sequentially vaccinated with BG505 SOSIP trimer variants: either BG505 SOSIP.664, which contains the T332N mutation (Sanders et al., 2013), or the further stabilized BG505 SOSIP.V4.1 (de Taeye et al., 2015), each administered either three or four times.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: BG505 SOSIP.664 contains the T332N mutation.
source: We used sera from rabbits sequentially vaccinated with BG505 SOSIP trimer variants: either BG505 SOSIP.664, which contains the T332N mutation (Sanders et al., 2013), or the further stabilized BG505 SOSIP.V4.1 (de Taeye et al., 2015), each administered either three or four times.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the BG505 SOSIP.664 construct, supported by a citation.

claim: BG505 SOSIP.V4.1 is a further stabilized version of BG505 SOSIP trimers.
source: We used sera from rabbits sequentially vaccinated with BG505 SOSIP trimer variants: either BG505 SOSIP.664, which contains the T332N mutation (Sanders et al., 2013), or the further stabilized BG505 SOSIP.V4.1 (de Taeye et al., 2015), each administered either three or four times.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the BG505 SOSIP.V4.1 construct, supported by a citation.

claim: Across all replicates, between 0.02% and 9.27% of the library escaped neutralization in mutational antigenic profiling experiments.
source: In our experiments, we chose serum concentrations to keep the average level of selection exerted by each serum relatively constant; across all replicates, between 0.02% and 9.27% of the library escaped neutralization, with the across-replicate averages for each serum ranging from 0.3% and 2.7% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mutational antigenic profiling experiments, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The across-replicate averages for each serum ranged from 0.3% and 2.7% of the library escaping neutralization.
source: In our experiments, we chose serum concentrations to keep the average level of selection exerted by each serum relatively constant; across all replicates, between 0.02% and 9.27% of the library escaped neutralization, with the across-replicate averages for each serum ranging from 0.3% and 2.7% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mutational antigenic profiling experiments, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The antigenic profiling results are largely concordant with prior knowledge on BG505 trimer immunogenicity in rabbits.
source: The results are largely concordant with prior knowledge on BG505 trimer immunogenicity in rabbits, with each serum targeting one or both of the C3/V5 or GH epitopes, which are indicated by blue and green, respectively, in Figure 2.
evidence: This is a comparison of the current results to prior knowledge, supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: Each serum targets one or both of the C3/V5 or GH epitopes.
source: The results are largely concordant with prior knowledge on BG505 trimer immunogenicity in rabbits, with each serum targeting one or both of the C3/V5 or GH epitopes, which are indicated by blue and green, respectively, in Figure 2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the mutational antigenic profiling, shown in Figure 2.

claim: The antigenic profiling largely agrees with the crude epitope specificities mapped using a small panel of pseudovirus point mutants.
source: Additionally, the antigenic profiling largely agrees with the crude epitope specificities mapped using a small panel of pseudovirus point mutants (Figure 1A, with mutations tested in preliminary TZM-bl assays plotted in black in Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a comparison of mutational antigenic profiling results to preliminary TZM-bl assay results, shown in Figures 1A and 2B.

claim: Most sera select neutralization-escape mutations in the C3/V5 epitope to some extent.
source: Notably, most sera select neutralization-escape mutations in the C3/V5 epitope to some extent, including sera from rabbit 2124, which appeared to predominantly target the GH based on the preliminary point-mutant mapping (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the mutational antigenic profiling data, shown in Figure 2.

claim: Sera from rabbit 2124 appeared to predominantly target the GH based on preliminary point-mutant mapping.
source: Notably, most sera select neutralization-escape mutations in the C3/V5 epitope to some extent, including sera from rabbit 2124, which appeared to predominantly target the GH based on the preliminary point-mutant mapping (Figure 1A).

claim: The fold enrichment in mutational antigenic profiling was well correlated with the fold change in ID50 in the neutralization assays (Pearson's r = 0.97, p value = 0.0011).
source: The fold enrichment in mutational antigenic profiling was well correlated with the fold change in ID50 in the neutralization assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 7, Pearson's r = 0.97, p value = 0.0011 from a two-tailed Pearson correlation test).
evidence: This is a statistical result comparing mutational antigenic profiling to TZM-bl neutralization assays, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: The 5724 escape profile is focused entirely on the C3/V5 epitope.
source: For example, the 5724 escape profile is focused entirely on the C3/V5 epitope: T464H is enriched ~190-fold in this serum's mutational antigenic profiling and shifts the ID50 64-fold in a TZM-bl neutralization assay (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a specific finding about serum 5724, supported by data in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: T464H is enriched ~190-fold in serum 5724's mutational antigenic profiling.
source: For example, the 5724 escape profile is focused entirely on the C3/V5 epitope: T464H is enriched ~190-fold in this serum's mutational antigenic profiling and shifts the ID50 64-fold in a TZM-bl neutralization assay (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from mutational antigenic profiling for serum 5724, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: T464H shifts the ID50 64-fold in a TZM-bl neutralization assay for serum 5724.
source: For example, the 5724 escape profile is focused entirely on the C3/V5 epitope: T464H is enriched ~190-fold in this serum's mutational antigenic profiling and shifts the ID50 64-fold in a TZM-bl neutralization assay (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from TZM-bl neutralization assays for serum 5724, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: Serum 2423 targets both the C3/V5 and GH epitopes.
source: In contrast, 2423 targets both the C3/V5 and GH epitopes (Figure 2), and the maximal effect mutant N356K has just a ≈2-fold effect in both mutational antigenic profiling and neutralization assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a finding about serum 2423, supported by data in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: The maximal effect mutant N356K has just a ≈2-fold effect in both mutational antigenic profiling and neutralization assays for serum 2423.
source: In contrast, 2423 targets both the C3/V5 and GH epitopes (Figure 2), and the maximal effect mutant N356K has just a ≈2-fold effect in both mutational antigenic profiling and neutralization assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a quantitative result for serum 2423, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: Across all sera, the binding responses identified by EMPEM include many epitopes where mutations do not affect viral neutralization.
source: Across all sera, it is immediately clear that the binding responses identified by EMPEM include many epitopes where mutations do not affect viral neutralization.
evidence: This is a primary finding comparing EMPEM and mutational antigenic profiling data, shown in Figure 3.

claim: For five of six sera, binding responses to both the GH and C3/V5 epitopes are observed by EMPEM.
source: For five of six sera, binding responses to both the GH and C3/V5 epitopes are observed.
evidence: This is a finding from EMPEM data, shown in Figure 3.

claim: All sera contain additional binding responses to other epitopes beyond GH and C3/V5.
source: All sera contain additional binding responses to other epitopes.
evidence: This is a finding from EMPEM data, shown in Figure 3.

claim: Serum 5724 contains binding responses to the GH, N611 glycan, base-of-trimer, and V1/V3 epitopes.
source: For example, even 5724, where we observe narrow, strongly focused viral escape in just the C3/V5 epitope, contains numerous additional binding responses, including the GH, N611 glycan, base-of-trimer, and V1/V3 epitopes.
evidence: This is a specific finding about serum 5724 from EMPEM data, shown in Figure 3.

claim: The base-of-trimer epitope is presented on recombinant trimers and commonly elicited by trimer immunization.
source: First, while the base-of-trimer epitope is presented on recombinant trimers and commonly elicited by trimer immunization (Bianchi et al., 2018; Cottrell et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2015), it is inaccessible in the replication-competent virus and hence does not elicit neutralizing antibodies.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The base-of-trimer epitope is inaccessible in replication-competent virus and hence does not elicit neutralizing antibodies.
source: First, while the base-of-trimer epitope is presented on recombinant trimers and commonly elicited by trimer immunization (Bianchi et al., 2018; Cottrell et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2015), it is inaccessible in the replication-competent virus and hence does not elicit neutralizing antibodies.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural accessibility of the base epitope on virus versus soluble trimers, supported by citations.

claim: Base-binding responses are observed in all sera by EMPEM.
source: Therefore, base-binding responses are observed in all sera, but of course are not mapped as neutralizing epitopes.
evidence: This is a finding from EMPEM data, shown in Figure 3.

claim: Binding responses to the N611 glycan region are observed in all sera by EMPEM.
source: Second, binding responses to the N611 glycan region are also observed in all sera (Figure 3), but we do not observe viral escape by disrupting this glycosylation motif (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a finding from EMPEM data, shown in Figure 3.

claim: Viral escape by disrupting the N611 glycosylation motif is not observed in mutational antigenic profiling.
source: Second, binding responses to the N611 glycan region are also observed in all sera (Figure 3), but we do not observe viral escape by disrupting this glycosylation motif (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a finding from mutational antigenic profiling data, shown in Figure 2.

claim: Site N611 is less glycosylated in BG505 SOSIP trimers than in virus.
source: It has been previously shown that site N611 is less glycosylated in BG505 SOSIP trimers than in virus, which enhances the immunogenicity of the exposed region when this glycan is missing (Derking et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Lower glycan occupancy at N611 in BG505 SOSIP trimers enhances the immunogenicity of the exposed region.
source: It has been previously shown that site N611 is less glycosylated in BG505 SOSIP trimers than in virus, which enhances the immunogenicity of the exposed region when this glycan is missing (Derking et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: gp120 interface responses are observed in two sera by EMPEM.
source: Third, gp120 interface responses are observed in two sera; both of these rabbits were immunized with BG505 SOSIP.v4 trimers.
evidence: This is a finding from EMPEM data, shown in Figure 3.

claim: Both rabbits with gp120 interface responses were immunized with BG505 SOSIP.v4 trimers.
source: Third, gp120 interface responses are observed in two sera; both of these rabbits were immunized with BG505 SOSIP.v4 trimers.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the immunization history of specific rabbits.

claim: The gp120 interface epitope includes the A316W stabilizing mutation added to SOSIP.v4.
source: This gp120 interface epitope includes the A316W stabilizing mutation added to the SOSIP.v4 to reduce the exposure of the V3 loop (de Taeye et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the SOSIP.v4 construct, supported by a citation.

claim: The A316W mutation was added to SOSIP.v4 to reduce the exposure of the V3 loop.
source: This gp120 interface epitope includes the A316W stabilizing mutation added to the SOSIP.v4 to reduce the exposure of the V3 loop (de Taeye et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the purpose of the A316W mutation, supported by a citation.

claim: The A316W mutation alters immunogenicity to the gp120 interface region, eliciting mutation-specific responses.
source: We have recently found that the A316W mutation alters immunogenicity to this region, eliciting mutation-specific responses to this region that would not cross-react with the A316-bearing viral libraries (manuscript in preparation).
evidence: This is a finding from unpublished work by the authors.

claim: Trimer-binding but non-neutralizing responses to the base, N611 glycan, and gp120 interface reflect antigenic differences between Env trimers and Env on the surface of virus.
source: Together, these trimer-binding but non-neutralizing responses to the base, N611 glycan, and gp120 interface reflect and expand on previously characterized antigenic differences between Env trimers to Env on the surface of virus (Bianchi et al., 2018; Cottrell et al., 2020; Derking et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: For both sera 5724 and 2425, single or multiple glycan knock in mutations to the GH epitope had negligible effects in TZM-bl neutralization assays.
source: For both 5724 and 2425, single or multiple glycan knock in mutations to the GH epitope had negligible effects, while single or multiple glycan knock in mutations to the C3/V5 epitope had large effects (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from TZM-bl neutralization assays, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: For both sera 5724 and 2425, single or multiple glycan knock in mutations to the C3/V5 epitope had large effects in TZM-bl neutralization assays.

evidence: This is a finding from TZM-bl neutralization assays, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: For sera 5724 and 2425, knocking in a glycan to each epitope (S241N + I358T) did not have much larger effects than the single C3 glycan knock in (I358T).
source: For these two sera, knocking in a glycan to each epitope (S241N + I358T) did not have much larger effects than the single C3 glycan knock in (I358T), suggesting these sera have limited GH neutralizing responses even after eliminating some of the C3/V5 directed neutralizing response.
evidence: This is a finding from TZM-bl neutralization assays, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sera 5724 and 2425 have limited GH neutralizing responses even after eliminating some of the C3/V5 directed neutralizing response.
source: For these two sera, knocking in a glycan to each epitope (S241N + I358T) did not have much larger effects than the single C3 glycan knock in (I358T), suggesting these sera have limited GH neutralizing responses even after eliminating some of the C3/V5 directed neutralizing response.
evidence: This is an inference based on TZM-bl neutralization assay data.

claim: GH binding responses observed in sera 5724 and 2425 are either non-neutralizing or much less dominant than the C3/V5 neutralizing antibody responses.
source: This suggests that these GH responses are either non-neutralizing or much less dominant than the C3/V5 neutralizing antibody responses.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of EMPEM and TZM-bl neutralization assay data.

claim: GH2-like binding responses have previously been identified in non-neutralizing sera using cryo-EMPEM.
source: Of note, while the resolution of the negative stain EMPEM in this present study limits fine epitope interpretations, GH binding responses (specifically 'GH2'-like responses) have previously been identified in non-neutralizing sera using cryo-EMPEM (Bianchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Sera 5727, 2124, 2214, and 2423 all displayed a greater effect for the double epitope glycan knock in mutations (S241N + I358T) than either of the single epitope knock in mutations.

claim: Sera 2423 had relatively equivalent neutralizing responses to both the GH and C3/V5 epitopes.
source: Comparing the effects of the single and double epitope mutations suggests sera 2423 had relatively equivalent neutralizing responses to both the GH and C3/V5 epitopes, sera 2124 and 2214 had a dominant response to GH and a subdominant response to C3/V5, and sera 5727 had a dominant response to C3/V5 and a subdominant response to GH (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: Sera 2124 and 2214 had a dominant response to GH and a subdominant response to C3/V5.

claim: Sera 5727 had a dominant response to C3/V5 and a subdominant response to GH.

claim: V1 insertions alone did not affect neutralization of any sera.
